quiz.q: In the hybrid model, where do the applications, connectors and logs live?
options: On the client's own servers (runtime plane)
quiz.explain: Hybrid = on-premises runtime + MuleSoft-provided control plane. Apps, connectors and logs stay on the client's servers; Runtime Manager and API Manager are in MuleSoft's cloud.

quiz.q: What can you do in hybrid that you can't in a pure on-premises setup (as described in class)?
options: Run more than one app per runtime
Deploy, start, stop and restart apps and the server from Runtime Manager
quiz.explain: In pure on-premises you log in to the server for everything; in hybrid you manage the apps from Runtime Manager while they run on your servers.

quiz.q: Where do you start registering an on-premises runtime with the control plane?
quiz.explain: Runtime Manager → Servers → Add server gives a name and shows a command (with a registration token) to run on the server.

quiz.q: Where do you run the command generated by Add server?
options: In the Mule runtime's bin directory on the server
quiz.explain: The command is run from the runtime's bin folder; it installs the Runtime Agent.

quiz.q: What does the Runtime Agent do?
options: Connects the Mule runtime to the control plane so apps can be managed from Runtime Manager
quiz.explain: The Runtime Agent establishes the connection between the runtime plane and the control plane.

quiz.q: How is communication between Anypoint Management Center and the Mule agent secured?
quiz.explain: It's authorised with two-way SSL: both sides authenticate each other and the traffic is encrypted.

quiz.q: During the live demo, the registered server showed status "Created" with only a Delete option. Why?
options: The connection wasn't established because registration failed with a certificate error
The trial account allows only CloudHub
quiz.explain: The command reported that the certificate from Anypoint Management Center was not valid, so no start/stop options appeared. Java 11 was confirmed compatible.

quiz.q: According to MuleSoft documentation checked in class, which Java versions does Mule 4.8 (Edge) support?
quiz.explain: Mule 4.8 supports Java 8, 11 and 17, so the machine's Java 11 wasn't the cause of the error.

quiz.q: How do you deploy an app to a registered hybrid server?
options: Runtime Manager → Deploy application → target Hybrid → select the registered server → upload JAR
Copy the JAR into the domains/ folder
quiz.explain: Runtime Manager sends the JAR through the established channel to the server's runtime, and status comes back to Runtime Manager.

quiz.q: In a typical company, who can start/stop apps in Prod and DR?
options: Only the responsible teams, e.g. production support
quiz.explain: Developers often get these options in lower environments; in higher environments only the responsible teams do.

quiz.q: You hit an unfamiliar error. What is the first step in the troubleshooting approach taught?
options: Read the error properly and check what it's connected to
quiz.explain: The order is: read the error → search (Google/docs/Help Center) → apply fixes → community → colleagues. Going to colleagues first increases dependency.

cards.back: Mule runtimes on your own servers, managed from MuleSoft's cloud control plane (Runtime Manager, API Manager).
On-prem: log in to the server for everything. Hybrid: deploy/start/stop/restart and view logs from **Runtime Manager**.
Adding an on-prem runtime to Runtime Manager: **Servers → Add server** → run the generated command in the runtime's `bin`.
Software installed in the Mule runtime that connects it to the control plane.
Mutual authentication with encrypted communication — used between Anypoint Management Center and the Mule agent.
Register server → install Runtime Agent (command in `bin`) → two-way SSL → start the runtime → server shows **Running**.
The control-plane services: Runtime Manager, API Manager, etc.
Central management via MuleSoft's control plane while keeping runtime, data and logs on your own infrastructure.
Runtime Manager → Deploy application → target **Hybrid** → choose the registered server → upload JAR → Deploy.
Failed with a **certificate error** ("possible man-in-the-middle attack"); server stuck at **Created**; unresolved in this session.

cards.front: Who registers servers in real projects?
cards.back: Usually admins / DevOps / architects set up environments; developers use them.
Lower environments: often developers. Prod/DR: only responsible teams such as **production support**.
Free community user-group events by region and city, online and offline.
A MuleSoft-enthusiast volunteer assigned by the community to run a group; you can apply.
MuleSoft Q&A / knowledge site; search errors or post questions. The instructor solves 60–70% of problems this way.
Robotic Process Automation / Intelligent Document Processing — other MuleSoft tools beyond this course.
**Read** the error → **search** docs/Help Center/Google → apply fixes → **community** → **colleague**.

cards.front: How much of MuleSoft does the course cover?
cards.back: The concepts used **80–85%** of the time in real projects, not the whole portfolio.
